annotations.title: The tenth day.
annotations.text: [1] Our Sauiour Chriſt inſtituting the Sacrament of the Euchariſt after the celebration of the Paſchal lambe, whiles they were at ſupper, the night before his death, thereby ſufficiently declared, that this old Paſch was a figure, not only of his Paſſion and Sacrifice on the Croſs, but alſo of that he then did ſo ſolemnly with his Apoſtles; whom alſo in that action he made Prieſts commanding them and their ſucceſſors to do the ſame in commemoration of him, til the end of the world. Other circumſtances likewiſe, and conference of the one with the other make it more clear, that as in ſome reſpects it more reſembled Chriſt's Paſſion and Sacrifice on the Croſs, ſo in others it more expreſſed the Euchariſt and myſtical commemoration of his death, though alſo in manie it prefigured Chriſt in both places [2]. For example, The preparing of the lambe the tenth day ſignified our Sauiours coming into Hieruſalem, the ſame tenth day of the firſt moone, now repreſented in the Church on Palm-Sunday. Alſo the choice qualities of the lambe, without ſpotte, a male, of the firſt yeare, foreshewed in general the puritie, fortitude, meeknes, and all perfection of the true Lambe of God, that taketh avvay the ſins of the vvorlde [3]. More particularly the killing & bereaving the Paſchal Lambe of natural life, the ſprinkling of his bloud on the dore poſts, the roaſting at the fire, & not breaking anie bone thereof, moſt ſpecially expreſſed Chriſt's death on the Croſs [4] [5]. But the fourtenth day, & the euening agree only with the Euchariſt [6], inſtituted the night before our Lords Paſſion, which he ſuffered the fiftenth being the ful moone) and at midday, as ancient S. Dionyſe of Ariopagite (in two Epiſtles, to Policarpus, & to Apollophanes) teſtifieth, admiring the miracle of the ſuns eclipſe, that happened the ſame time. Neither did the eating of the Lambe directly prefigurate the oblation on the Croſs, for Chriſt was not crucified to be eaten: but the Sacrament in forms of bread and vvine was expreſly figured by eating the lambe with vnleauened bread, & drinking the cuppe thereto adioyned (Luc. 22. v. 17.) In like ſorte the Lambe immolated in commemoration of the deliuerie of Iſrael from death, & from ſeruitude, when the firſt-born of Ægypt were ſlaine, moſt aptly prefigured the Euchariſt, which is a perpetual commemoration of man's redemption & deliuerie from eternal death, and from bondage of the devil & ſinne, by Chriſt's death on the Croſs, which death indeed was the very redemption & deliuerie of mankind, & not a commemoration thereof. Finally, the immolating of the Lambe vvithin the houſe with preciſe commandment to carie nothing thereof forth, pertained particularly to the Euchariſt, which our Lord celebrated within the houſe, whereby S. Cyprian (lib. de vnit. Eccles.) proueth, that the B. Sacrament muſt not be giuen to anie out of the Catholic Church, though Chriſt's Paſſion be extended to all the world, as wel to bring ſuch as are without into the Church, as to ſaue thoſe that are already entered in. [7] In this ſorte the moſt ancient and beſt expoſitors of holie Scripture, explicate this ſpecial figure of the Paſchal Lambe. As we shal here produce ſome witneſſes in confirmation of this truth. [8] Tertulian lib. 4. contra Marcionem, expounding our Sauiours words [9]: With deſire I haue deſired to eate this Paſch with you before I ſuffer, ſaith, Chriſt coueted not veruecinam Iudæorum, the mutton of the Jews, but profeſſing that with deſire he deſired to eate the Paſch, as his owne (for it was vnmete that God should couete anie thing not his owne) the bread which he took, and gaue to his diſciples, he made his owne body, ſaying: This is my body, that is, a figure of my body. Figura autem non fuiſſet, niſi veritatis eſſet corpus: But it had not bene a figure (ſaith he) vnles it were a body of veritie, or, a verie body, to wit, not phantaſtical as the heretic Marcion imagined; becauſe the figures in the old Teſtament were not figures, except a true body anſwered vnto them. So the Sacramentaries ſenſe, that Tertullian ſhould call the Euchariſt a figure, is quite againſt his meaning, and maketh him conclude nothing againſt Marcion; whereas his whole drift is, by the figures of the old Teſtament to proue, that in the Euchariſt is the true & real body of Chriſt, & that conſequently Chriſt hath a true and real body. Origen (in 26. Mat.) teacheth that in the great parlor (where Chriſt did eate the Paſchal Lambe) he alſo made his new Paſch. [10] S. Cyprian (de Cæna Dom.) ſaith: In the ſupper of ſacramental banquets, old & new Inſtitutions met together. The lambe being conſumed, which old tradition propoſed, the Maſter ſetteth inconſumptible meate to his diſciples. S. Gregorie Nazianzen (orat. 2. de Paſcha) ſaith God commanded the Paſchal Lambe ſhould be eaten in the euening, becauſe Chriſt in the euening gaue the Sacrament of his owne body to his diſciples. S. Hierom (in 26. Mat.) After that the figuratiue Paſch was complete, & Chriſt had eaten the flesh of the lambe with his Apoſtles, he taketh bread, which confirmeth the heart of man [11], and paſſeth ouer to the true Sacrament of Paſch. Likewiſe S. Chryſoſtom (Ho. de prodit. Iudæ) ſaith: In the ſame table both the Paſchs, of the figure, & of the veritie were celebrated. S. Ambroſe (in Lucæ. 1.) expreſly applieth this figuratiue lambe to the Euchariſt, as it is celebrated in the Church, by himſelf & other Prieſts [12], ſaying: When we ſacrifice, Chriſt is preſent, Chriſt is ſacrificed: for Chriſt our Paſch is immolated [13]. The like affirmeth S. Auguſtine (li. 2. cont. lit. Petil. c. 27.) It is another Paſch that the Jews celebrated of a ſhepe, another which we receiue in the body & blood of our Lord. S. Leo (ſer. 7. de Paſs.) To the end shadows might give place to the body, & figures might ceaſe in preſence of the veritie, the old obſervation is taken away by the new Sacrament, hoſte paſſeth into hoſte, blood excludeth blood, and when the legal feſtiuitie is changed, it is fulfilled. [14] S. Gregorie (ho. 22. in Evang.) proueth by theſe words, You shal not eate thereof anie thing raw, that beſides the letter there is a ſpiritual ſenſe. Behold (ſaith he) the verie words of the hiſtory driue vs from the hiſtorical vnderſtanding. For did the Iſraelitical people in Ægypt vſe to eate a lambe raw, that the law should nede to ſay: you shal not eate it raw? And ſo in that homilie this great Doctor explicateth how we ought to celebrate & receiue the Sacrament of the Euchariſt, by the figure of this Paſchal lambe. This blood (ſaith he) is ſprinkled on both poſts, when the Sacrament of his Paſſion is receiued with mouth, to redemption, and meditated with intentiue mind to imitation, & in the tranſome ouer the dore, when pure intention directeth the exterior act, alſo when we carie the Croſs of his Paſſion in our forehead. The flesh of the lambe is eaten at night, becauſe we now receiue our Lords body in the Sacrament, when yet we ſee not each others conſciences, roaſted at the fire, when we ioyne to our belief good works of feruent charity: with vnleauened bread & with lettuce, that is, in ſinceritie, without corruption of vaine glory, and with bitter penance for ſins: not raw, nor ſod in water, to wit, neither eſteeming Chriſt a mere man, nor conſidering of him, with human vviſdome or priuate ſpirite of heretics, called ſtollen water (Prov. 9.) To deuoure the head vvith the feete and entrails, is by faith to believe the Diuinitie of Chriſt, and to imitate by loue the ſteps of his humanitie, & greedily to learne all Chriſtian myſteries. Nothing is left til morning, when we endeavour in this life before the reſurrection to know euerie point of Chriſtian doctrin, ſo farre as to vs pertaineth. But if anie thing be left, it muſt be burned in the fire, becauſe thoſe hard & higheſt myſteries, which we cannot vnderſtand, we muſt remitte to the Holie Ghoſt, leſt anie proudly preſume either to contemne, or to proclaime that he vnderſtandeth not. [15] He further deſcribeth alſo what maner of perſons are to eate this new Paſch. Their loins muſt be gyrded, that is, all carnal pleaſures tamed. They muſt haue shoes on their feete, by the good examples of former Saints dead before, muſt ſtrengthen their ſteps, to flee from vice, and follow virtue: holding ſtaues in their hands, to rule and ſtay themſelues and others from ſliding, by the ſtaffe of authoritie. They muſt eate the Paſch ſpeedily, that is without delay or procraſtination muſt learne the myſteries of man's redemption, and heauenlie life, and ſo performe Gods will & precepts, in this life with ſpeede. To this effect S. Gregorie diſcourſeth at large in the moral ſenſe, which we haue abridged, and otherwiſe (though holie Scripture be ful hereof) ſeldome touch. Returning therefore to our particular purpoſe, in all theſe teſtimonies we ſpecially vrge, that the paſchal lambe was a figure, not only of Chriſt's Paſſion, but alſo of the Euchariſt. VVhereupon, beſides the often expreſs mention of our B. Sauiours body and blood in the ſame, which Proteſtants would wreſt (as they do alſo the ſame terms in holie Scripture) to figuratiue ſenſe, [16] it neceſſarily followeth, that there be farre more excellent contents in the Sacrament of the Euchariſt, then natural bread and wine. For S. Paul teacheth (colloſs. 2.) that as the body excelleth the shadow, ſo the veritie, or thing figured excelleth the figure. Whereas the ſubſtance of bread and wine doth not excel, much leſſe ſo farre excel the Paſchal Lambe, as by S. Pauls doctrine is required. Againe, ſeing the Paſchal lambe was a Sacrifice [17], as appeareth in this Chap. v. 6. & 27. alſo Num. 9. v. 7. & 13. and Mar. 14. v. 12: and as it was immolated was a figure of the Euchariſt, as before appeareth by conference of the one with the other, in reſpect of the time, place, maner of offering, and eating it, and by teſtimonie of the Doctors aboue cited, it followeth alſo that the Holie Euchariſt is a Sacrifice farre excelling the figure.
